chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Abdullah ibn Talha, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who died and left much wealth, and left a mother who was a slave and a sister who was a slave. He said: 'They are bought from the wealth of the deceased, then they are emancipated and they inherit.' I said: 'What do you think if the owners of the slave-girls refuse, what is to be done?' He said: 'It is not for them to refuse, and they are evaluated at a just price, then what is due to them is given according to the price.'

I said: 'What do you think if they were bought, then emancipated, then they inherited him, who would inherit them afterwards?' He said: 'The freedmen of their son would inherit them, because they were bought from the wealth of the son.'
ai.seo_question: How are slave mothers and sisters emancipated and inherited from a deceased man's estate in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the jurisprudential procedure for emancipating slave mothers and sisters left by a deceased man, establishing that their manumission is funded from the estate and that owners cannot refuse sale if a just valuation is provided. It further clarifies the inheritance dynamics, noting that if the slaves are purchased from the son's share, their mawali (manumission bond) attaches to the son, illustrating the Shia principle of linking legal status to the source of financial settlement.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Ja’far, from Abdullah Bin Talha, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who died and left a lot of wealth, and left a mother who was a slave, and a sister who was a slave. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They should be bought from the wealth of the deceased, and they would both inherit (the remainder)’. I said, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view if the people (owner) of the slaves refuse, how should it be dealt with?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is not for them (to refuse), and they would both be evaluated with a just price, then they (masters) would be given what is for them in accordance with the price’.

I said, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view if they are both bought, then emancipated (liberated), then inherit him, who would be the ones who would be inheriting the two of them afterwards?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They would both be inherited by the guardians of their son (the deceased) because they had both been bought from the wealth of the son’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn Ja‘far from ‘Abd Allah ibn Talhah who has narrated the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who dies leaving behind a large amount of assets, a mother and a sister who are owned by someone. He (the Imam) said, ‘They are bought with the assets of the deceased, set free and made to inherit him.’ I then asked, ‘What happens if the people of the slave-girl refuse?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘They cannot do so. They are appraised fairly, then their fairly appraised value is paid.’

I then asked, ‘What happens if they are bought, set free then made to inherit the deceased; if they die who will inherit them?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The Mawali (relatives) of her son will inherit them because they were bought with the legacy of the son.’”
